high_config.portrait: You run as a quiet production engine. A demand comes in — a deadline, a spec someone else wrote — and instead of negotiating it away you sit down and metabolize it: the month stem Xin as Eating God sits beside the strong Ji earth day master, and hidden Xin in the day branch You means the craft is literally under your feet, so the first working version appears while others are still confirming requirements. The pressure arrives through the year stem Yi as Seven Killings, and hidden Bing fire in both Snake branches buffers it into method before it lands raw. You answer hard tasks with finished objects, teach by demonstrating rather than lecturing, and repair things instead of writing reports about them. Crucially, in high-spec mode you price the work: because you know the loop tends to end at the delivered object, you state a rate, a title, or a named credit before absorbing the next demand. Peers get your reliability — if you said Friday, it is Friday — but the finished work also carries your name upward, and money conversations happen because you initiate them.
observable_signals: The work speaks, but so does the invoice. After a delivery you can point to something banked — a fee, a credit line, a title change — not just a thank-you and a bigger follow-up task. This runs against the chart's grain: Direct Wealth carries zero weight and water is absent from every visible character, so this signal only appears because you build the habit deliberately.

You still absorb hard demands without drama, but the ratio shifts: a portion of your Eating God output — the heaviest force in the chart — goes into your own projects, not only other people's specs. In practice: some weeks contain work that exists because you decided it should exist.

Peers and juniors come to you not just to hand off the hard task, but to learn how you break it down. The Direct Resource layer — that hidden Bing fire converting pressure into method — becomes something you teach, which turns your buffer from a private cost into a visible asset.

low_config.portrait: The same engine runs, but the exhaust goes nowhere. You still deliver — the Eating God is too strong to shut off — but each finished piece converts into the next, larger demand rather than into money, position, or anything banked for yourself. Direct Wealth carries zero weight and water, the element that would carry Wealth for you, is missing from all eight visible characters, so in low-spec mode nobody — including you — ever names what the work is worth. You retreat further into the horizontal axis: Companion weight is jointly heaviest, from the hour stem Ji matching your day master plus hidden earth stacked in the branches, so problems get solved by doing them yourself or splitting them with trusted equals, never by routing them upward. Rob Wealth, the muscle that would fight for resources, sits at a mere two, so negotiation stays unpracticed and the room where your work is priced stays a room you never enter. This is not failure or misery — the work is still excellent. It is the same structure running closed-loop: pressure in, craft out, recognition tightens the pressure, repeat.
observable_signals: Your calendar fills with other people's priorities. Look at last month: nearly every significant block of your Eating God output answered someone else's spec, and the deliverables carry their names, not yours.

When asked what something costs — a rate, a timeline trade, a scope cut — you answer with the work itself ('I'll just get it done') rather than with terms. The Direct Officer channel is empty and the Wealth family carries almost nothing, so without practice the pricing sentence simply never forms.

Your strongest relationships are all lateral: teammates, peers, people who work next to you. You have no practicing relationship with anyone who decides budgets or promotions, because Companion-mode comfort quietly replaced the vertical axis.

environment.enables: Environments where finished craft is visible and priced. A place where the person who delivers also gets named credit, a rate, or a title — where the loop's far end is wired to a return channel. Because the ten years beginning around age forty-two run a water branch (Zi), and the ten years after that another (Hai), water — the missing carrier of Wealth — finally flows into the structure; in those stretches, environments built on explicit terms, contracts, and prices let the chart open fully. Small teams with direct access to the decision-maker also suit you: your Companion-heavy wiring works best when the equal next to you can also approve the budget.
environment.suppresses: Environments that reward the negotiation you don't practice and ignore the objects you produce: large hierarchies where price and promotion are decided two levels above you, where Eating God output disappears into someone else's report, and where the only recognized skill is managing upward — your empty Direct Officer channel. Also suppressive: places with no peers of your own level, because your heaviest force operates horizontally and starves without equals. In such settings the loop closes: pressure flows in through Seven Killings, the work flows out, and nothing flows back.

belief.limiting_belief: 'Good work speaks for itself — asking about money or title cheapens it.' A second one rides along: 'I can handle it, so I should take it.' Both feel like virtue, which is why they hold.
belief.origin: Both are byproducts of the defensive abilities. Silent over-absorption grows from the pressure-to-buffer wiring: Seven Killings at the year stem pushes demands in, Direct Resource softens them, and the strong self holds the load — so refusing or pricing a demand never occurs to you as an option, only absorbing it. Peer-circle retreat grows from Companion being jointly heaviest: your default trust lives with equals, and the vertical axis — Direct Officer empty, Rob Wealth thin, Indirect Wealth nearly absent — was never exercised, so 'negotiating upward' came to feel foreign, even slightly dishonorable.
belief.ceiling_effect: The belief closes the loop's return channel manually. The chart already shows Wealth nearly weightless and water absent; believing that pricing is beneath you means you never build the one bridge the structure lacks. Result: the more impressive your delivery record, the heavier the next demand, and the thinner your own reserves — recognition converts into load instead of standing. The ceiling isn't talent; it's that the finished object is the only sentence you let yourself speak.

awareness.key_moment: The switch point arrives the day you notice the pattern inside a single episode: you just delivered something excellent, felt briefly lighter — Eating God release — and then, within days, a bigger request arrived from the same source with the same non-terms. The moment of lucidity is seeing the request not as praise but as the loop tightening. One clear signpost outside: as the water-branch decades approach — the stretch starting around age forty-two — terms-and-price conversations begin to feel less foreign. That easing is the chart telling you the return channel can open.
awareness.what_to_notice: Notice what you feel when asked 'what do you want out of this?' If the honest inner answer is 'just that it gets done well', the leak is active. Notice whether your name appears on your outputs anywhere a decision-maker could see it. And notice the physical pattern: the quiet satisfaction at finishing followed by the small drop when the next demand lands unchanged — that drop is the unconverted energy leaving the system.

early_warnings: The follow-up arrives before the thanks fades. You deliver a hard piece, and within the same week the same person hands you a larger one at the same undefined terms. Track this in your messages for a month — if the ratio of demands-after-deliveries keeps rising while terms stay flat, the loop is tightening.

Your 'own projects' queue has not moved. There is a list somewhere — a thing you meant to build, teach, or fix for yourself — and it has been untouched for weeks while every block of your craft time went to other people's specs. Your heaviest force is being consumed servicing incoming pressure rather than feeding you.

You cannot say your number. Someone asks what you charge, or what the trade should be for extra scope, and you deflect with effort ('I'll manage it') or with silence. If a full month passes without you stating a single price, term, or credit request out loud, the vertical channel has gone dormant again.
switch_actions: Institute the pre-absorption gate. Before accepting any new hard demand, write one line: what you get beyond the work being done — a rate, a named credit, a title, a scope boundary. If the honest answer is nothing, negotiate one item before saying yes. This directly patches the leak: pressure still converts to craft, but the loop now passes through a return point.

Book one vertical conversation per fortnight. Identify one person who decides budgets, promotion, or pricing, and take fifteen minutes — not to complain, but to present a finished piece of your Eating God output and ask directly how work like it gets valued where you are. This exercises the channels the chart left nearly empty: the formal-authority axis and the resource-fighting muscle.

Reclaim a fixed slice of craft time for your own output. Block two hours weekly that cannot be assigned to anyone's spec — a prototype, a write-up, a demonstrated method — and put your name on whatever comes out. This redirects the heaviest force in your chart from pure pressure-service into assets that stay yours, rebuilding the loop's far end from the output side.
